chapter.li: LEChapter6 Verse1 And in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Greeks against the Hebrews because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration. VerseEnd Verse2 Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them and said, It is not acceptable that we should leave the word of God and serve tables. VerseEnd Verse3 Wherefore, brethren, seek out among you seven men of honest report, full of the holy ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business; VerseEnd Verse4 but we will give ourselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word. VerseEnd Verse5 And the saying pleased the whole multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the holy ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas (a convert of Antioch) VerseEnd, Verse6 whom they set before the apostles. And when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them. VerseEnd Verse7 And the word of God increased, and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly, and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith. VerseEnd

Verse8 And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people. VerseEnd Verse9 And there arose certain of the synagogue who are called Libertines, and also Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of them of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing with Stephen. VerseEnd Verse10 And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spoke. VerseEnd Verse11 Then they suborned men who said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and against God. VerseEnd Verse12 And they stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, and came upon him and caught him, and brought him to the council, VerseEnd Verse13 and set up false witnesses who said, This man ceases not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place and the law, VerseEnd Verse14 for we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place and shall change the customs which Moses delivered us. VerseEnd Verse15 And all that sat in the council, looking steadfastly on him, saw his face as if it were the face of an angel. VerseEnd

LEChapter7 Verse1 Then said the high priest, Are these things so? VerseEnd Verse2 And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelled in Haran, VerseEnd Verse3 and said unto him, Get yourself out of your country and from your kindred, and come into the land which I shall show you. VerseEnd Verse4 Then he came out of the land of the Chaldeans and dwelled in Haran. And from there, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land wherein you now dwell, VerseEnd Verse5 and he gave him no inheritance in it; no, not so much as to set his foot on. Yet he promised that he would give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him — when as yet he had no child. VerseEnd Verse6 And God spoke in this way: that his seed should sojourn in a strange land, and that they should bring them into bondage and treat them evil four hundred years. VerseEnd Verse7 And the nation to whom they shall be in bondage will I judge, said God; and after that, they shall come forth and serve me in this place. VerseEnd Verse8 And he gave him the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begot Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begot Jacob, and Jacob begot the twelve patriarchs. VerseEnd Verse9 And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt; but God was with him, VerseEnd Verse10 and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house. VerseEnd

Verse11 Now there came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers found no sustenance; VerseEnd Verse12 but when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first. VerseEnd Verse13 And at the second time, Joseph was made known to his brethren, and Joseph’s kindred were made known unto Pharaoh. VerseEnd Verse14 Then Joseph sent and called his father Jacob to him, and all his kindred — seventy-five souls. VerseEnd Verse15 So Jacob went down into Egypt and died, he and our fathers, VerseEnd Verse16 and were carried over into Shechem, and laid in the sepulcher that Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem. VerseEnd

Verse17 But when the time of the promise drew near, which God had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt VerseEnd Verse18 until another king arose who knew not Joseph. VerseEnd Verse19 The same dealt subtly with our kindred and evil treated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children to the end they might not live VerseEnd — Verse20 in which time Moses was born, and was exceedingly fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months. VerseEnd Verse21 And when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son. VerseEnd Verse22 And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. VerseEnd Verse23 And when he was fully forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel. VerseEnd Verse24 And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him and avenged him who was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian, VerseEnd Verse25 for he supposed his brethren would have understood that God by his hand would deliver them. But they understood not. VerseEnd Verse26 And the next day, he showed himself unto them as they quarreled, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, you are brethren; why do you do wrong one to another? VerseEnd Verse27 But he that did his neighbor wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made you a ruler and a judge over us? VerseEnd Verse28 Will you kill me as you did the Egyptian yesterday? VerseEnd Verse29 Then Moses fled at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Midian, where he begot two sons. VerseEnd

Verse30 And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush. VerseEnd Verse31 When Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight, and as he drew near to behold it, the voice of the Lord came unto him, VerseEnd Verse32 saying, I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Then Moses trembled and dared not behold. VerseEnd Verse33 Then said the Lord to him, Put off your shoes from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground. VerseEnd Verse34 I have seen, I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send you into Egypt. VerseEnd

Verse35 This Moses, whom they refused — saying, Who made you a ruler and a judge? — the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer, by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush; VerseEnd Verse36 he brought them out after he had shown wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness forty years. VerseEnd Verse37 This is that Moses who said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall you hear. VerseEnd Verse38 This is he that was in the church in the wilderness, with the angel who spoke to him in the mount Sinai and with our fathers, who received the living oracles to give unto us VerseEnd — Verse39 whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt, VerseEnd Verse40 saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we know not what has become of him. VerseEnd Verse41 And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands. VerseEnd Verse42 Then God gave them up to worship the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: O you house of Israel, have you offered to me slain beasts and sacrifices by the space of forty years in the wilderness? VerseEnd Verse43 Yea, you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of your god Remphan, figures which you made, to worship them; and I will carry you away beyond Babylon. VerseEnd

Verse44 Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness — as he had appointed, speaking unto Moses that he should make it according to the pattern that he had seen VerseEnd — Verse45 which also our fathers that came after brought in with Joshua, into the possession of the Gentiles whom God drove out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David, VerseEnd Verse46 who found favor before God and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob. VerseEnd Verse47 But Solomon built him a house. VerseEnd Verse48 Nevertheless, the Most High dwells not in temples made with hands, as says the prophet: VerseEnd Verse49 Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool; what house will you build me? — says the Lord. Or what is the place of my rest? VerseEnd Verse50 Has not my hand made all these things? VerseEnd

Verse51 You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you do always resist the holy ghost; as your fathers did, so do you. VerseEnd Verse52 Which of the prophets have your fathers not persecuted? And they have slain them who showed before of the coming of the Just One, of whom you have been now the betrayers and murderers, VerseEnd Verse53 who have received the law by the disposition of angels and have not kept it. VerseEnd

Verse54 When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart and they gnashed at him with their teeth. VerseEnd Verse55 But he, being full of the holy ghost, looked up steadfastly into Heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, VerseEnd Verse56 and said, Behold, I see the Heavens opened and the Son of Man standing on the right hand of God. VerseEnd Verse57 Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, VerseEnd Verse58 and cast him out of the city, and stoned him; and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man’s feet, whose name was Saul. VerseEnd Verse59 And they stoned Stephen; and he, calling upon God, said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. VerseEnd Verse60 And he kneeled down and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge! And when he had said this, he fell asleep. VerseEnd LEChapter8 Verse1 And Saul was consenting unto his death.
